document.abstract: Video compression technologies, such as MPEG-2, are now standardized, and a number of video codecs based on these standards are being developed in many organizations, for use in digital television broadcast and transmission services. The degradation in picture quality produced by video compression is so complicated for human eyes to evaluate that neither a simple signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) nor detailed objective assessment parameters are accurate for this measurement. Studies on picture quality assessment have been conducted based on human visual perception models, which have led to an applicable modeling of the visual process.

authors.affiliation: KDD Research and Development Laboratories Inc., Tokyo, Japan
authors.bio: Takahiro Hamada received B.S. and Ph.D. degrees in electrical engineering from Tokyo University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1985 and 1997, respectively, and the M.S. degree in electrical engineering from California Institute of Technology, Pasadena in 1989. —Since 1987, he has been with the Research and Development Laboratories of KDD (Overseas Telecommunication Co. Ltd. of Japan), Tokyo, Japan, and has worked on the development of digital coding of broadcast TV and high-definition TV signals. His research interests include transform coding and quantization for high quality and highly efficient television signal coding. His work in these areas has resulted in the development of a Japanese coding standard for an enhanced wide screen TV (EDTV II). Hamada is currently engaged in research on picture quality assessment technologies.

authors.bio: Satoshi Miyaji received B.S. and M.S. degrees in electronics from Waseda University, Tokyo, Japan, in 1993 and 1995, respectively. Since 1995, he has been with KDD Research and Development Laboratories Inc., and has worked on the development of digital coding for very low bit-rate video and picture quality evaluation systems. Currently, Miyaji is a research engineer in the Visual Communications Laboratory of KDD Research and Development Laboratories Inc.
authors.name: Satoshi Miyaji

authors.affiliation: KDD Research and Development Laboratories Inc., Tokyo, Japan
authors.bio: Shuichi Matsumoto received B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in electronics from Hokkaido University, Sapporo, Japan, in 1977, 1979, and 1990, respectively. — Since 1979, he has been with Research and Development Laboratories of KDD (Overseas Telecommunication Co., Ltd. of Japan), Tokyo, Japan, and has worked on the development of digital coding for broadcast TV and high-definition TV signals. He is a rapporteur in charge of digital coding standards in Study Group 9 of ITV-T. Currently, he is a Senior Manager at the Visual Communications Laboratory of KDD Research and Development Laboratories Inc. — Dr. Matsumoto received the 1983 Best Paper Award and the 1986 Sinohara Memorial Award from IEICE Japan.
